projects.name: ShadowComm
projects.headline: Covert Asynchronous Communication Protocol (Architecture & Design Phase)
projects.description: Architectural blueprint and protocol specifications for a covert, metadata-resistant communication channel over non-standard transport sockets.
projects.problemStatement: Standard network communication exposes traffic packet sizes and timing characteristics, allowing adversaries to perform statistical traffic correlation even on encrypted streams.
projects.purpose: Research and specify transport morphing and packet padding protocols that resist heuristic metadata correlation.
projects.targetUsers: Security researchers exploring protocol covert channels.
keyCapabilities: Protocol frame specifications for traffic padding normalization
Diffie-Hellman ephemeral handshake protocol design
Threat model against passive timing correlation attacks
projects.architectureOverview: Designed as a client-server daemon architecture with customizable transport covert carriers.
projects.myContribution: Formulated protocol specification, state transitions, and cryptographic requirements.
technicalChallenges: Minimizing protocol latency while inserting random dummy packets to defeat timing correlation.
projects.limitations: Repository is in architectural research phase; code implementation actively being finalized.
futureWork: Release initial C++ socket multiplexer prototype with synthetic packet pacing.

projects.name: MediQueue
projects.headline: Real-Time Hospital Queue Orchestration & Patient Throughput Platform
projects.description: Full-stack healthcare queue management system utilizing React, TypeScript, Supabase PostgreSQL, and WebSockets to optimize patient intake and consultation workflows.
projects.problemStatement: Hospital outpatient departments experience chaotic bottlenecks, opaque wait times, and high receptionist administrative burdens due to manual token and queue handling.
projects.purpose: Provide a synchronized, three-portal system (Patient, Doctor, Administrator) that calculates dynamic wait times and coordinates patient flow in real time.
projects.targetUsers: Hospital outpatient clinics, attending physicians, intake staff, and arriving patients.
keyCapabilities: Role-based portal architecture: Patient Token Tracker, Doctor Consultation Desk, Hospital Administrator Console
Real-time WebSocket event propagation for live token position changes
Estimated wait time calculation based on historical consultation durations per department
Doctor consultation lifecycle management: Call Next, In Consultation, Complete, No Show
Automated queue prioritization for urgent medical triage cases
projects.architectureOverview: React client with role-based routing connecting to Supabase for Postgres relational storage, Row-Level Security (RLS) policies, and real-time WebSocket channel subscriptions for queue state broadcasts.
projects.systemFlowDiagram: Patient Booking -> Token Generation -> Supabase Realtime Channel -> Doctor Desk Call -> Patient Notification
projects.myContribution: Engineered the Doctor and Patient real-time views, configured database schemas and RLS security policies, and implemented token queue state machines.
technicalChallenges: Handling concurrent token requests without race conditions in token counter increments under heavy intake load.
Maintaining persistent WebSocket subscriptions across mobile browsers during intermittent cellular connectivity drops.
projects.limitations: Currently designed for single-facility operations; multi-hospital federation requires tenant isolation schema changes.
futureWork: SMS and WhatsApp gateway webhooks for token updates without requiring an active browser tab.
Predictive AI consultation duration forecasting using historical patient acuity metrics.

projects.name: SecretSnap
projects.headline: Secure Ephemeral Messaging Platform with Client-Side AES-256
projects.description: A privacy-focused communication system providing client-side AES-256 encryption, zero server-side storage, and automated message self-destruction timers.
projects.problemStatement: Standard messaging applications frequently store plaintext or recoverable message metadata on centralized databases, exposing user communication to subpoena, data breach, and passive traffic inspection.
projects.purpose: Provide a disposable, zero-trace transmission channel where cryptographic operations are performed solely in client memory, and ciphertext self-destructs upon viewing or TTL expiration.
projects.targetUsers: Security professionals, privacy advocates, and individuals needing tamper-evident, ephemeral payload exchanges.
keyCapabilities: In-browser AES-256-GCM symmetric payload encryption
Deterministic client-side key derivation via PBKDF2 with SHA-256
Configurable Time-To-Live (TTL) countdown triggers
Zero-knowledge server model (server acts as ephemeral relay only)
Single-view burn-after-reading verification hash
projects.architectureOverview: The client application generates an ephemeral 256-bit key in memory via the Web Crypto API. The message payload is encrypted with an initialization vector (IV) and transmitted alongside an integrity MAC. The decryption key is embedded in the URL fragment (#), ensuring the server never observes the secret key.
projects.systemFlowDiagram: Client -> WebCrypto(AES-GCM) -> Encrypted Blob -> Relay Dispatch -> Recipient -> Key Fragment Hash -> Instant Burn
projects.myContribution: Engineered the client-side cryptographic pipeline, stateful self-destruction timer, memory wipe routines, and responsive dark-mode interface.
technicalChallenges: Preventing cryptographic key leakage through browser history and URL query strings by restricting key material strictly to the URI fragment identifier.
Guaranteeing reliable memory sanitization upon message destruction within JavaScript's non-deterministic garbage collection lifecycle.
projects.limitations: Client-side encryption cannot prevent recipient physical screen capture (shoulder surfing or external cameras). Requires modern browser supporting the Web Cryptography API.
futureWork: Implementation of WebAssembly-based post-quantum Kyber key encapsulation.
Optional steganographic image container encoding for covert carrier transmission.

projects.name: PRISM — Predictive Risk Modeling Framework
projects.headline: CUDA-Accelerated Deep Learning Framework for Predictive Risk Assessment
projects.description: High-throughput machine learning pipeline implemented in Python 3.12 and PyTorch with hardware-accelerated CUDA execution for predictive risk modeling.
projects.problemStatement: Predictive risk modeling across high-dimensional feature spaces frequently suffers from training bottlenecks, non-convergent gradients, and poor GPU memory utilization.
projects.purpose: Provide a high-throughput, modular deep learning framework optimized for multi-feature anomaly detection, risk quantification, and rapid matrix inference.
projects.targetUsers: Data scientists, risk intelligence analysts, and computational research teams.
keyCapabilities: CUDA 12.1 native GPU kernel acceleration with automated device fallback
Modular deep neural network architecture with customizable loss formulations
Feature scaling, normalization, and outlier truncation preprocessing pipeline
Automated evaluation telemetry with confusion metrics and ROC-AUC assessment
projects.architectureOverview: Python 3.12 pipeline structured with decoupled dataset loaders, PyTorch nn.Module architectures, CUDA memory caching, and checkpointed training epochs with tensor validation.
projects.systemFlowDiagram: Data Ingestion -> Tensor Pipeline -> CUDA Kernel Allocation -> Backprop / Loss Minimization -> Risk Prediction Engine
projects.myContribution: Engineered the PyTorch neural network layer architecture, CUDA device initialization checks, evaluation metrics logging, and data preprocessing scripts.
technicalChallenges: Resolving CUDA driver memory fragmentation when batch processing disparate high-variance tensor structures.
Balancing precision vs inference latency for real-time risk classification loops.
projects.limitations: Maximum training throughput is bounded by available VRAM on single-GPU hardware configurations.
futureWork: Implement FP16 mixed-precision training via PyTorch AMP (Automatic Mixed Precision).
Export inference graph to ONNX runtime for deployment on low-power edge gateways.

projects.name: Shadow Message Cipher
projects.headline: Encrypted Real-Time Terminal Communication Suite with Multimedia Attachments
projects.description: Production-grade React + TypeScript secure messaging platform featuring end-to-end client-side encryption, encrypted voice/camera attachments, and terminal-grade interface ergonomics.
projects.problemStatement: Most secure communication platforms restrict payloads to plain text or rely on heavy native binaries that require complex OS privileges.
projects.purpose: Deliver an in-browser encrypted communication suite supporting multimedia streams (camera captures, voice notes, binary files) with minimal runtime overhead.
projects.targetUsers: Security teams and engineers requiring private ad-hoc data exchange channels.
keyCapabilities: Full client-side payload encryption for multimedia blobs and audio buffers
Direct camera and microphone capture directly into in-memory cipher streams
Real-time cipher verification and authentication state machine
Session self-wipe and local cache isolation
projects.architectureOverview: Constructed with modular React state containers driving WebRTC / MediaStream capture nodes. Audio and image streams are converted to Uint8Array binary buffers, passed through an AES cipher transformer, and packaged into chunked frames for transmission.
projects.systemFlowDiagram: MediaStream -> Uint8Array Buffer -> AES Stream Transform -> Frame Dispatch -> Symmetric Decrypt -> Render
projects.myContribution: Authored the media stream capture hooks, binary buffer serialization, encrypted chunk delivery mechanism, and terminal aesthetic UI components.
technicalChallenges: Synchronizing encrypted audio chunk reconstruction across asynchronous browser event loops without introducing audible jitter or distortion.
Managing memory consumption when encrypting high-resolution camera frames entirely in browser heap memory.
projects.limitations: High resolution video encryption can experience frame drops on resource-constrained mobile hardware due to JavaScript single-threaded crypto loop overhead.
futureWork: Offload crypto transformations to dedicated Web Workers to ensure 60fps UI responsiveness during bulk multimedia encryption.
Add multi-party encrypted room topologies.

projects.name: SpellSense
projects.headline: Research-Grade NLP Spelling Intelligence & Algorithmic Benchmarking Suite
projects.description: Production-level multi-page NLP platform empirically comparing TextBlob, SymSpell, and edit-distance algorithms with real-time empirical latency and accuracy telemetry.
projects.problemStatement: Most spelling correction engines operate as black boxes, preventing computational linguists from inspecting algorithm trade-offs between Levenshtein distance, Damerau-Levenshtein, and n-gram corpus frequency lookups.
projects.purpose: Provide an interactive, empirical comparative workbench that quantifies algorithmic execution latency, memory footprint, and correction accuracy across varying error profiles.
projects.targetUsers: Computational linguistics students, NLP researchers, and search-query ranking engineers.
keyCapabilities: Side-by-side algorithmic correction comparing TextBlob probabilistic models against SymSpell Symmetric Delete algorithms
Levenshtein and Damerau-Levenshtein matrix computation visualization
Real-time telemetry showing execution time in milliseconds and candidate rank confidence
Modular multi-page application with isolated empirical benchmark routes
projects.architectureOverview: Multi-page frontend built with React and TypeScript communicating with NLP correction algorithms. Includes stateful telemetry stores that record latency distributions, candidate scoring curves, and phonetic matching distances.
projects.systemFlowDiagram: Input Corpus -> Tokenizer -> Edit Distance Transform -> Candidate Ranking Engine -> Comparative Telemetry Visualizer
projects.myContribution: Architected the multi-page client application, integrated algorithmic benchmark telemetry, implemented Levenshtein computation matrices, and designed visual telemetry charts.
technicalChallenges: Visualizing dynamic dynamic-programming matrices (Levenshtein table) in real-time without causing rendering lag on paragraph-length text inputs.
Normalizing scoring metrics between SymSpell frequency counts and TextBlob probabilistic language model outputs.
projects.limitations: Corpus vocabulary size is constrained in browser runtime mode; deep morphological inflection requires server-side model hosting.
futureWork: Incorporate BERT/transformer-based masked language modeling for context-aware homophone correction (e.g. 'their' vs 'there').
Add phonetic Soundex and Metaphone distance comparisons.
